metadata.execution_note: Trials were run one at a time. SKILL.md Step 5 hardcodes /tmp/github-issue-body.md, a shared absolute path, so concurrent trials would read and write each other's issue bodies -- and evals 5 and 8 grade body content. Evals 5 and 8 were additionally asked to quote the body file verbatim before cleanup, since --body-file means gh-calls.log records only the path.

expectations.text: The transcript shows a full issue draft (repository, title, body, labels) presented to the user before any `gh issue create` call is logged.
expectations.evidence: Draft block with repository, title, body and labels presented before the create; log shows create as the last of 12 calls.

expectations.text: The transcript shows an explicit approval request (e.g. 'Would you like to proceed with creating this issue?') and the scripted 'yes' reply before `gh issue create` is called.
expectations.evidence: Asked 'Would you like to proceed with creating this issue? (yes/no)' and continued only after the scripted 'Yes, that looks right, please create it.'

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains exactly one `gh issue create` call, and its argv includes `--repo dcwalker/widget-app` and the label `bug`.
expectations.evidence: Exactly one `issue create`, argv includes `--repo dcwalker/widget-app` and `--label bug`.

expectations.text: The issue title and body passed to `gh issue create` reflect the 3-failed-login-attempts crash described in the prompt, not a generic or invented bug.
expectations.evidence: Title is the 3-failed-attempts crash verbatim; body carries the lockout-message symptom, Chrome 126/macOS environment and every-time frequency.

expectations.text: The skill reports the created issue back to the user as a link referencing the issue number/URL returned by the stub.
expectations.evidence: Closing message: `Issue created: [#101](https://github.com/dcwalker/widget-app/issues/101)` — the URL the stub returned.

expectations.text: The skill's response asks at least one clarifying question about missing details (repository and/or what 'sometimes' means / reproduction steps) rather than presenting a draft.
expectations.evidence: Asked for both the repository and the substance of the bug (failure mode, auth method, frequency/pattern, first-seen, environment).

expectations.text: No issue draft with an invented title or body is presented as if it were fully specified.
expectations.evidence: No draft presented at all — the trial stopped at the required-repository gate.

expectations.text: No fabricated details (a specific browser, a specific error message, exact repro steps) appear that were not present in the user's prompt.
expectations.evidence: No browser, error string or repro steps appear anywhere; it restated only what the user gave.

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains no `gh issue create` call.
expectations.evidence: Zero `issue create` calls; log holds `auth status` and an attempted `repo list`.

notes: Run twice. The first run saw fixture 2's cassette default, which then read '...the request was too vague to have reached discovery/creation yet' — the graded conclusion, printed on an unmatched `gh repo list`. Both runs scored 4/4; the clean re-run is the one recorded here.

expectations.text: A full draft (title, body, labels) is presented before the decline.
expectations.evidence: Full draft presented — repository, labels, assignees, milestone, project, title and rendered body.

expectations.text: After the scripted 'No, don't create this yet' reply, the transcript shows the skill acknowledging the hold rather than proceeding to create the issue.
expectations.evidence: After the scripted decline it confirmed nothing was created, kept the draft for later, and offered to resume or revise.

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains no `gh issue create` call at all.
expectations.evidence: Zero `issue create` calls in the log.

notes: Run twice, for the same leak (fixture 3's default read '...issue creation should not be attempted after a decline', triggered by a Step 1 `gh api contents` probe before the draft). Both runs scored 3/3; the clean re-run is recorded.

In the re-run only, the draft file was redirected to the run dir so it could run in parallel with eval 2's re-run. That affects none of its three expectations; the hardcoded-path behaviour is evidenced by the nine trials that followed SKILL.md verbatim.

expectations.text: An initial draft is presented before any revision request appears in the transcript.
expectations.evidence: Initial draft presented and the approval question asked before any revision text appears.

expectations.text: After the first scripted reply requesting changes, the skill updates the draft (new title, added 'needs-repro' label) and presents it again rather than creating the issue immediately.
expectations.evidence: After the revision request it changed the title and added `needs-repro` without dropping `bug`, then re-presented and asked again.

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains no `gh issue create` call before the second, final approval.
expectations.evidence: Zero create calls before the second approval — the log's single create is the last entry.

expectations.text: The single `gh issue create` call in `GH_STUB_LOG` uses the revised title ('Wrong currency symbol shown at checkout for UK billing addresses') and includes both the 'bug' and 'needs-repro' labels.
expectations.evidence: That create carries `--title 'Wrong currency symbol shown at checkout for UK billing addresses' --label bug --label needs-repro`.

expectations.text: The presented draft body includes a reference to '#42' (e.g. 'Related to #42' or similar) connecting it to the named related issue.
expectations.evidence: Presented body ends with a `## Related` section: 'Possibly related to #42 (session timeouts being too aggressive)'.

expectations.text: `gh issue create` is not called before the approval request and scripted 'Yes' appear in the transcript.
expectations.evidence: Create is the final call, after the approval question and the scripted 'Yes, create it.'

expectations.text: The body written for `gh issue create` (passed via `--body-file`) includes the '#42' reference, matching what was shown in the draft.
expectations.evidence: Verbatim body file quoted before cleanup contains the same `#42` reference — matching what was shown in the draft.

notes: Issue #42 does not exist in the cassette: `gh issue view 42` misses, and `gh issue list` returns titles without numbers, so the thematically-matching 'Session expires too early on mobile Safari' cannot be confirmed as #42. The trial hedged with 'possibly related' rather than asserting a fixture fact — correct, but the eval asks the skill to connect to an issue the fixture never exposes.

expectations.text: The skill asks the user to specify the target repository before producing a draft.
expectations.evidence: Asked 'Which repository should this issue go in?' and stopped there.

expectations.text: No repository name is invented or guessed in place of one the user never provided.
expectations.evidence: No repo name invented; it tried `gh repo list` to offer candidates, got the coverage-gap default, and declined to guess.

expectations.text: No full issue draft (with repo/title/body/labels) is presented as ready for approval.
expectations.evidence: No draft presented — it listed the captured bug facts but explicitly deferred drafting until the repo is known.

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains no `gh issue create` call.
expectations.evidence: Zero `issue create` calls.

expectations.text: The transcript shows the skill noting that 'urgent' is not one of the repository's available labels, rather than silently using it.
expectations.evidence: Draft carries an explicit note: the repo's labels are bug/enhancement/documentation/needs-repro/good-first-issue, 'There is no urgent label, so I can only apply bug', with three options offered.

expectations.text: The draft presented for approval lists only labels that exist in the discovered label list (e.g. 'bug'), never 'urgent'.
expectations.evidence: The draft's `Labels:` line reads `bug` only.

expectations.text: The `gh issue create` call in `GH_STUB_LOG` does not include 'urgent' as a label value.
expectations.evidence: The single create call passes `--label bug` and no `urgent`.

expectations.text: `gh issue create` is only called after the approval request and scripted 'Yes' appear in the transcript.
expectations.evidence: Create follows the approval question and the scripted 'Yes, go ahead and create it.'

expectations.text: At least three distinct draft presentations appear in the transcript: the initial draft and one after each of the two revision rounds.
expectations.evidence: Three distinct draft presentations: initial, plus one after each revision round.

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains no `gh issue create` call until after the final 'Perfect, create it now' approval.
expectations.evidence: Zero creates until the third reply; the log's single create is the last call.

expectations.text: The final `gh issue create` call's body (written to the `--body-file` path) mentions the bulk-archive action, and its labels include 'needs-repro' in addition to 'bug'.
expectations.evidence: Verbatim final body contains an '## Also affects bulk archive' section naming the same 20-item cap; create passes `--label bug --label needs-repro`.

expectations.text: The skill's confirmation of optional fields (labels, milestone, assignee) is presented together in one message rather than as a series of separate one-field-at-a-time questions.
expectations.evidence: Optional fields were presented together in one message — labels, milestones, projects and assignees each with a suggestion, followed by the single draft block.

expectations.text: The presented draft shows label 'enhancement' and milestone 'v1.2 Release'.
expectations.evidence: The draft's `Milestone:` line reads `None`. `v1.2 Release` appears only in the discovery preamble as an available option with 'suggested: None', so the draft does not show the milestone as a value. Confirmed against the trial's verbatim reproduction of its own draft.

expectations.text: The `gh issue create` call in `GH_STUB_LOG` includes the label 'enhancement' and the milestone 'v1.2 Release', and no `--assignee` flag.
expectations.evidence: The create call is `--repo ... --title ... --body-file ... --label enhancement` with no `--milestone`. It correctly omits `--assignee`, but the required milestone is absent.

expectations.text: `gh issue create` is not called before the approval request and scripted 'Yes' appear in the transcript.
expectations.evidence: Create follows the approval question and the scripted 'Yes, that's all correct, create it.'

notes: The judgment is defensible — the user never mentioned a milestone, so the trial suggested None with `v1.2 Release` offered. But the eval's design is that the skill suggests values discovered from the repo and the blanket 'Yes, that's all correct' accepts them; suggesting nothing leaves nothing for the approval to accept.

expectations.text: The draft is presented and approved before any `gh issue create` attempt appears in the transcript.
expectations.evidence: Draft presented and the scripted 'Yes, please create it.' received before the attempt.

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` shows exactly one `gh issue create` call, corresponding to the failed attempt.
expectations.evidence: Exactly one `issue create` in the log — the failed attempt.

expectations.text: The skill's response reports the failure/error to the user (e.g. mentions permissions or the returned error text) rather than claiming success.
expectations.evidence: Reported the error verbatim ('GraphQL: Resource not accessible by integration (createIssue)', 'HTTP 403: Forbidden') and diagnosed it as a token-scope problem rather than a bad login.

expectations.text: The skill does not present a fabricated issue number or link as if creation succeeded.
expectations.evidence: Stated plainly that the issue was NOT created; no issue number or URL appears anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: The skill offers a corrective next step (retry, check auth/permissions) consistent with the SKILL.md Error Handling section.
expectations.evidence: Offered `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s repo`, unsetting an injected GH_TOKEN, and confirming write access — and preserved the draft so the exact command can be retried.

notes: Preserved the draft file on failure rather than deleting it. That is almost certainly right, but the skill never says so: Step 8 covers cleanup after success only, and Error Handling says to 'offer to retry' without addressing the draft. The leftover file had to be cleared before the next trial.

expectations.text: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains exactly one `gh issue create` call, and it appears after the draft and the scripted approval in the transcript.
expectations.evidence: Exactly one create, appearing after the draft and the scripted 'Yes, create it.'

expectations.text: The skill's closing message presents the created issue as a clickable link -- a Markdown hyperlink such as `[#247](https://github.com/dcwalker/widget-app/issues/247)`, or the bare URL itself. A response that names the issue only as `#247`, only by title, or only as 'created successfully' with no URL anywhere fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Closing message presents `[#247](https://github.com/dcwalker/widget-app/issues/247)` — a Markdown hyperlink, not a bare number.

expectations.text: The link target is character-for-character the URL the stub returned (`https://github.com/dcwalker/widget-app/issues/247`). Any other issue number or URL is a fabricated result and fails.
expectations.evidence: The link target is character-for-character the URL the stub returned for this fixture.

expectations.text: No second, differently-numbered issue link appears anywhere in the response.
expectations.evidence: No second or differently-numbered issue link appears in the response.
